turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hey Lawrence how're you doing

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'm doing alright aside from this elbow pain

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So it looks like here that you came in to see us today for an evaluation of that right elbow pain can you tell me can you can you tell me well first of all what do you think has been causing that pain

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So I really during this pandemic I really got into ceramics and doing pottery so I've been doing a lot of pottery and over the past week I then started to develop this elbow pain

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay and then so tell me a little bit more about that elbow pain where does it hurt exactly

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: You know it hurts a lot in the inside of my elbow

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay so the inside of your right elbow okay

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And then does the pain radiate down your arm or up into your shoulder or anything like that

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It doesn't go into my shoulder it's it stays mostly at my elbow but it can go down a bit into my forearm

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay and then do you remember any trauma did you hit your arm or elbow or any on anything

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No nothing I I really was trying to think if there is anything else and I can't think of anything

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay and you've never injured that right elbow before

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright so now let's talk a little bit about your pain and how bad it how bad is that pain on a scale from zero to ten ten being the worst pain you've ever felt in your life

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say probably a six

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay and does that pain keep you up at night

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It does

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay and when you have that kind of pain does it keep you from doing other type of activities

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah I mean I still try to like work through with using my arm but yeah it's it's it's difficult for me sometimes to lift and do things because of that pain

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay and then and how long has this pain been going on

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: About four days now

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright and anything you've done to help relieve or alleviate that pain any anything that that's giving you relief

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've tried ibuprofen that helps a little but not much

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay so if it's okay with you I would like to do a a quick physical exam your vitals look good and I'm gon na do a focused exam on that right elbow I'm gon na go ahead and and and press here do you do you have any pain when I press here

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes I do

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay so you are positive for pain to palpation you do note that moderate tenderness of the medial epicondyle now I'm gon na have you turn your wrist as if you're turning a door knob do you have any pain when you do that

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not really

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay now turn your wrist in so do you have any pain when you do that

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah that hurts

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay so you do have pain you were positive for pain when you pronate that that that forearm okay I'm gon na go ahead and have you rest your arm on the table here palm side up now I want you to raise your hand by bending at the wrist and I'm gon na put some resistance against it do you have any pain when I press against your flexed wrist

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes I do

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright so you are positive for pain with resistance against flexion of that left wrist so I let let's go ahead and review the x-ray that we did of your elbow the good news is I don't see any fracture or bony abnormality of that right elbow which is good so let's talk a little bit about my assessment and plan for you so for the problem with elbow pain I do believe that this is consistent with medial epicondylitis which is caused by the overuse and potential damage of those tendons that bend That that bend the wrist towards the palm now I want you to rest it I'm gon na order a sling and I want you to wear the sling while you're awake now we're also gon na have you apply ice to the elbow for twenty minutes three times a day and I want you to take ibuprofen that's gon na be six hundred milligrams q.6 h. With food and I want you to take that for a full week now you're not gon na like this part but I want you to hold off for the next couple of weeks on doing any type of pottery work okay alright now what I wan na do is I wan na see you again in a week and I wan na see how you're doing okay

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Alrighty

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alrighty so I'll have the nurse come in and get you set up with that sling and I will see you again in about a week

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Alright thank you

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Thank you
